Miscellaneous First Appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of MV Act praying to set-aside the impugned Judgment and Award dated 02.03.2020 passed in M.V.C. No.911/2018 on the file of learned III Addl. Small Causes Judge & MACT, Bengaluru (SCCH-18), allow the claim petition in M.V.C. No.911/2018 on the file of learned III Addl. Small Causes Judge & MACT,
Bengaluru, (SCCH-18), awarding a compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest as this Hon'ble Court deems fit, to the appellant herein and to pass such other order/s as this Hon'ble Court deems fit to grant under the circumstances of the case, in the interest of justice and equity.
This Miscellaneous First Appeal coming on for Hearing through Physical Hearing/Video Conference, this day the Court delivered the following :
JUDGMENT

The present appeal is filed by the claimant under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
challenging the dismissal of his claim petition by the learned III Addl.Small Causes Judge and Addl.Chief Metropolitan Magistrate and Member, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru (SCCH-18), (hereinafter for brevity referred to as 'the Tribunal'), by the judgment and award dated 02.03.2020, passed in M.V.C.No.911/2018.
2.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The summary of the case of the present appellant as claimant before the Tribunal was that, on the date 23.01.2017, at about 6.00 p.m., while he was proceeding as a pillion rider on a TVS XL Super motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-18-Y-5636, along with his friend one Veerabhadraiah, who was the rider and moving on Pura Road towards Kodihalli, the driver of a luggage Autorickshaw bearing registration No.KA-18-B-7416, being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner,
dashed against his motorcycle, as a result of the said road traffic accident, the appellant fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Kadur.

After the first-aid treatment there, he was shifted to Kasturba Hospital at Manipal, wherein he was treated Sri. Shadaksharaiah vs Smt. Shankaramma on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157133327/
2 as an inpatient.
The claimant contends that, till the date of filing, the claim petition he has been taking treatment in the said hospital as an out-patient and has incurred huge expenses towards medical treatment.

With this, he has prayed for compensation of a sum of `15 lakhs from the respondents before the Tribunal arraying them as respondent Nos.1 and 2 respectively as the owner and insurer of the alleged offending luggage Autorickshaw.
3. In response to the notices served upon them, the respondents appeared through their counsel and filed their statement of objections.
Both the respondents in common have taken a contention in their statement of objections that the road traffic accident as contended by the claimant has not taken place in the manner as alleged.

They denied that the claimant suffered any injuries in the road traffic accident, more particularly, they denied the alleged involvement of the alleged luggage Autorickshaw bearing registration No.KA-18-B-7416.

The respondent No.2 further contended that a false charge sheet has been filed against the driver of the said luggage Autorickshaw by falsely implicating the said Autorickshaw, when in fact, even according to the claimant, the alleged offending vehicle was a Milk Van.
With this, the respondents prayed to dismiss the claim petition.

4. Based on the pleadings of the parties, the Tribunal has framed the following issues :
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Luggage Auto-rickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-18-B-7416 (Policy No.3379/01169981/
000/01) on 23-1-2017 at about 6.00 P.M. Kodihalli Road, Chikkamagaluru?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate?
From whom?
3. What order or award?
5. In support of his claim petition, the claimant got examined himself as PW-1 and got examined one Sri Girish and one Dr.Nagaraj B.N., as PW-3 and got marked documents from Exs.P-1 to P-26.

From the respondents' side, one Sri Murthy C., an official from General Hospital, Kadur, was examined as RW-1, who has deposed only to the extent of producing the medical records maintained in the Government Hospital, Kadur and marked them from Exs.R-1 to R-3.

From the side of respondent Nos.2-Insurance Company, one Sri Kruthishree N., its Legal Officer,
was examined as RW-2.

The documents from Exs.R-1 to R-5 were marked from the respondents'
side.
6. After hearing the arguments addressed before it, the Tribunal by its impugned judgment, while answering issue No.1 in the negative, proceeded to dismiss the claim petition of the claimant.
It is challenging the said judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the claimant before the Tribunal has preferred the present appeal.

3 7.
The respondent No.2 herein (insurer) is represented by its counsel.
Though notice to respondent No.1 was served, but, he has remained unrepresented.
8. Records from the Tribunal pertaining to the matter were called for and the same are placed before the Court.
9. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for respondent No.2- Insurance Company.

Perused the materials placed before this Court, including memorandum of appeal, impugned judgment and records of the Tribunal.
10.
The learned counsel for the appellant/claimant in her argument submitted that the delay in filing the complaint was solely for the reason that the claimant himself was admitted in the hospital.
There was none in his family to go to the police and lodge a complaint.
Further, the claimant was taking treatment at a distant hospital at Manipal, as such, the delay caused is not intentional and would not affect the interest of either of the parties in any manner.
She further contended that the offending vehicle was a luggage Autorickshaw bearing registration No.KA-18-B-7416, but, not the Milk Van.

However, the Tribunal without considering the documents from Exs.P-1 to P-9, which were the documents, including the charge sheet filed by the police after due investigation, has proceeded to attribute its own imaginary reasons and answered issue No.1 in the negative.

With this,
learned counsel for the appellant/claimant prayed for allowing the appeal and to remand the matter back to enable the Tribunal to give its finding on issue Nos.2 and 3.
11.

Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2- Insurance Company in his arguments submitted that at the earliest point of time, when the claimant was taken to the hospital, it was stated before the doctor that it was a Milk Van which has caused the road traffic accident.

He further submitted that there is a vast difference between a Milk Van and a luggage Autorickshaw and one can by naked eye, differentiate between these two vehicles, as such, there cannot be any confusion with regard to nature of the vehicle causing the road traffic accident.
He also submitted that the delay in filing the complaint has not been properly explained by the claimant.
It is considering these aspects, since the Tribunal has answered issue No.1 in the negative, the same does not warrant any interference at the hands of this Court.
12. The claimant who got himself examined as PW-1 has reiterated the contentions taken up by him in his claim petition, even in his examination-in-chief also.

To support his contention that the road traffic accident is caused due to the rash and negligent driving by luggage Autorickshaw by its driver, he has got produced and relied upon the copies of FIR, scene of offence panchanama, sketch of the spot of the offence, three photographs, wound certificate and the charge sheet, which he has got them marked from Exs.P-2 to P-9.
13.

A perusal of the complaint and FIR at Ex.P-1 would go to show that complaint with respect to the alleged road traffic accident was filed on the date 30.01.2017 by one Sri Veerabhadraiah, son of Chandraiah, before Yagati Police Station in Kadur Taluk.

According to - 10 - Sri. Shadaksharaiah vs Smt. Shankaramma on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157133327/
4

sentences.text: the complainant, as well the claimant, the date of alleged road traffic accident was on 23.01.2017, as such, there was seven days delay in filing the complaint before the police.

According to the Tribunal,
it was eight days delay.
The complainant in his very complaint itself has stated that, since the injured was to be taken to the hospital and his medical care was to be given priority, the same was attended to on priority.

He has specifically stated that, he was the rider of the motorcycle at the time of the accident and it was him who had to take the injured to Kadur hospital in the beginning and from there, for higher treatment, to the hospital at Manipal.

In his complaint, he has stated that,
since he was engaged in attending to the injured at Manipal Hospital for all those days, there was delay in he coming to the police station and lodging the complaint.
14.
The case of the claimant was also that, he was a pillion rider on the motorcycle on which the complainant in Ex.P-1 was riding.

Even claimant has also stated that,
- 11 - he sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
In his cross-examination, PW-1 has stated that while he was being taken to hospital, said Veerabhadraiah was also accompanying him in the ambulance.
Therefore, the complainant's version and the complaint at Ex.P-1 that he was busy in attending the injured in the hospital at Manipal, as such, the delay is caused, cannot be doubted or suspected.

15. No doubt, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 in his argument submitted that when the hospital at Kadur, where the patient was initially taken at first, was informed about a road traffic accident and it noted the same in its Medico-Legal Case Register, there was no possibility of delayed registration of the complaint since the police were required to visit the hospital and record the statement of the complainant.

The said argument of learned counsel for respondent No.2 though prima facie appears to be convincing, however, in the instant case, the fact remains that,
- 12 - immediately after giving him the first-aid treatment, the claimant was referred to a higher medical centre for higher treatment.
As such, the claimant was taken to Kasturba Hospital at Manipal, which admittedly was at a distant place and in a different District.

As such, merely because the police have not gone to the said Kasturba Hospital, Manipal, and have not recorded the statement of the claimant, by that itself, the delay caused in filing the complaint, cannot be suspected, since the reason given by the complainant in the very complaint at Ex.P-1 appears to be bona fide and convincing.

As such, the contention of learned counsel for respondent No.2 that the Tribunal has rightly appreciated the aspect of delay in lodging the complaint as one of the reason for rejecting the claim petition, is not acceptable.

16. The main reason for which the Tribunal proceeded to answer the issue No.1 in the negative and which is also the bone of contention in this appeal is about the alleged involvement of luggage Autorickshaw bearing Sri. Shadaksharaiah vs Smt. Shankaramma on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157133327/
5 - 13 - registration No.KA-18-B-7416 in the road traffic accident and as an offending motor vehicle.

The learned counsel for respondent No.2 in his argument while reiterating the observations made by the Tribunal in the impugned judgment submitted that the Medico-Legal Case Register extract at Ex.R-3, which is produced by RW-1, mentions that the patient (claimant) was brought to the hospital with the history of road traffic accident which was a collision between TVS Scooter and lorry (Milk Van) near Yagati.

It is banking upon the said recording of the nature of the vehicle as Milk Van, learned counsel for respondent No.2 vehemently submitted that the luggage Autorickshaw, which is shown as the offending motor vehicle, is purely an after thought and due to an act of collusion between the claimant and owner of TVS XL Super motorcycle and the owner of the said luggage autorickshaw with the police.

Per contra, learned counsel for the appellant in her argument contended that, admittedly the informant about - 14 - the history of the accident before the doctor at the Government Hospital, Kadur, was not the claimant.
Even the respondents have also not stated that who was the complainant before the said doctor.

Merely because the nature of the vehicle is shown to be a Milk Van and when there was no basis for such an entry in Medico-Legal Case register as Milk Van, it cannot be held that, it was the Milk Van that has caused the road traffic accident.

She further contended that there is nothing on record to prevent anyone identifying the offending luggage Autorickshaw bearing registration No.KA-18-B-7416 also as a Milk Van since there is no definition of what constitutes a Milk Van.

Further, highlighting an entry made in the Medico- Legal Case Register and drawing the attention of the Court to the said aspect of recording of the registration number of the offending vehicle in the Medico-Legal Case Register, learned counsel for the appellant stated that when the Medico-Legal Case Register shows the registration number - 15 - of the offending vehicle, the description of the vehicle becomes immaterial.
17.
I find more force in the argument of learned counsel for the appellant.
There is nothing in the Medico- Legal Case extract at Ex.R-3 as to who was the informant to the doctor about the history of the road traffic accident.
Even the claimant in his cross-examination as PW-1 also has stated that it was not him who gave the details to the doctor and he is also not aware whether it was Sri Veerabhadraiah.

As such, in the absence of any particular details as to the informant about the history of road traffic accident before the doctor, merely because the nature of the vehicle is shown to be a Milk Van, it cannot be considered that it was the Milk Van alone which has caused the accident.

This observation gains more force for the reason that, the very same Medico-Legal Case Sri. Shadaksharaiah vs Smt. Shankaramma on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157133327/
6 record at Ex.R-3 clearly mentions the registration number of the alleged offending vehicle as KA-18-B-7416.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Undisputedly, the registration number of the alleged offending vehicle - 16 - which is shown to be a luggage Autorickshaw, whose photographs are also produced at Ex.P-4, is also KA-18-B-7416.
Therefore, merely based upon the nature of the offending vehicle shown in the Medico-Legal Case register, the claimant's case cannot be disbelieved.

Secondly, the complaint at Ex.P-1 and a thorough investigation conducted by the police, during the process of which, they have visited the scene of offence and got the alleged vehicles involved in the road traffic accident inspected and examined by the Motor Vehicle Inspector and got its report and after concluding the investigation, have filed the charge sheet against the driver of the luggage Autorickshaw bearing registration No.KA-18-B- 7416, but, not filed a `B' report or a charge sheet against the driver of the alleged Milk Van, would clearly go to show that the offending vehicle involved in the road traffic accident was not the alleged Milk Van, the details about which are not known to either of the parties, but, it was - 17 - the luggage Autorickshaw bearing registration No.KA-18-B-7416.
18.

The Motor Vehicle Inspector's report at Exs.P-5 and P-6 also shows the damages caused to both,
luggage Autorickshaw and the TVS XL motorcycle upon which the claimant was said to be traveling as a pillion rider at the time of road traffic accident.
Those documents also corresponds to a collision between the said luggage Autorickshaw and TVS XL motorcycle.

As such also, the observation of the learned Judge of the Tribunal that the involvement of the luggage Autorickshaw bearing registration No.KA-18-B-7416 in the road traffic accident is doubtful, is not acceptable.
19. The evidence of PW-1, PW-2 and the medical evidence of PW-3 would go to show that the claimant sustained multiple injures in the accident.

The wound certificate issued by the Government Hospital at Kadur, where the claimant was taken immediately after the road traffic accident mentions that the radiological report has - 18 - revealed that the claimant had sustained distal femur fracture of the left leg and fracture of left ulna and left scapula fracture.
The doctor has opined that all these three injuries are grievous in nature.

20. Hence, it is established that the road traffic accident in question has occurred on the date, time and place as contended by the claimant in the claim petition and the said accident has taken place solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the luggage Autorickshaw bearing registration No.KA-18-B-7416 by its driver.

However, without appreciating the evidence placed before it in its proper perspective, since the Tribunal has answered issue No.1 in the negative, the said finding Sri. Shadaksharaiah vs Smt. Shankaramma on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157133327/
7 deserves to be set aside and issue No.1 is required to be answered in the affirmative.

sentences.text: 21. The Tribunal after answering issue No.1 in the negative, did not proceed to give its reasoned finding on issue No.2 which was about entitlement of compensation.
Since the Tribunal has not answered issued No.2 and - 19 - both side learned counsels also prays that parties would agitate and address their arguments before the Tribunal on issue No.2

, I am of the view that the impugned judgment deserves to be set aside and the matter requires to be remanded to the Tribunal to give its finding on issue Nos.2 and 3.
22.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER [i] The Appeal filed by the claimant stands allowed in part;
[ii] The impugned judgment and award passed by the learned III Addl.Small Causes Judge and Addl.Chief Metropolitan Magistrate and Member, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru (SCCH-18), dated 02.03.2020, in M.V.C.No.911/2018, is set aside.
[iii] The matter is remanded to the learned III Addl.Small Causes Judge and Addl.Chief Metropolitan Magistrate and Member, Motor - 20 - Accidents Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru (SCCH-18), to give its finding on issue Nos.2 and 3 and to dispose of the matter in accordance with law, however, taking issue No.1 as answered in the affirmative.
